title: Robust deep learning based protein sequence design using ProteinMPNN
layout_note: Panel A (top, full width): on the left a rendered two-chain cartoon (chain A pink, chain B green) above a sketch of two residues' backbone atoms (N, Ca, C as pink and green triangles joined by dashed distance lines) and a peach 'Input' box; in the middle a large light-blue rounded container titled 'ProteinMPNN' holding two white rounded sub-containers side by side (Backbone Encoder, Sequence Decoder); on the right Probabilities -> an 'Iterative decoding' circle -> Sample -> Sequence -> a peach 'Output' box. Panels B and C below are details: B contrasts fixed left-to-right decoding with ProteinMPNN's decoding order on numbered cell grids, C ties positions across three chains with lines from a cartoon to per-chain grids.
grouping: Nested containers: the light-blue outer panel for the model, white rounded panels for the encoder and the decoder. Input and output are peach rounded boxes with bold 'Input:' / 'Output:' prefixes outside the model. Chain identity is carried by colour: every feature grid is split into a pink part and a green part, matching the two chains of the input cartoon. A small legend in B keys the cell colours (grey decoding order, green fixed amino acids, yellow / blue context not used / used).
shapes_depth: Node and edge features are small grids of square cells (edges as multi-row grids, nodes as single rows), pink cells for chain A and green for chain B; '3x' beside a dashed loop arrow marks repeated layers. Thick black elbow arrows, flat fills, no shadows. Structures (input in A, three-chain example in C) are rendered translucent cartoons; the atom sketch uses small black and blue dots with letter labels.
proposed_highlight: The model is the single large tinted container with its name in large type at the top; input and output sit outside it in a contrasting peach, and the decoding-order idea gets its own panel (B) with numbered cells.
lesson: Carry chain identity through every tensor: colour each chain once in the input cartoon and then split every node and edge feature grid into the same two colours, so multi-chain conditioning reads without labels.
notes: Venue = bioRxiv preprint: the PDF header reads 'this version posted June 4, 2022' (v1; venue_source: pdf); no journal version was checked. The figure is one embedded raster in the PDF, so photo_share is null and the rendered cartoons enter the palette.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
